title: Uniform presentability and bounded representatives for simplicial-category diagrams
statement:
Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small ordinary category $D$, and an uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ with $|\operatorname{Mor}D|<\kappa$. Regular means unions of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ have size less than $\kappa$. A category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\kappa$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Locally $\kappa$-presentable means cocomplete and generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects. Use simplicial categories and arbitrary enriched functors as in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Define the size of a simplicial category $A$ to be the cardinality of the disjoint union of its objects and all sets $A(a,b)_n$, over all ordered pairs of objects and $n\geq0$.

For every containing universe $\mathcal V$, the ordinary categories $\mathrm{sCat}_{\mathcal V}$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathrm{sCat}_{\mathcal V})$ are locally $\kappa$-presentable. A simplicial category is $\kappa$-presentable exactly when its size is less than $\kappa$. A $D$-diagram is $\kappa$-presentable exactly when all its values are $\kappa$-presentable. Every diagram is the colimit of a $\mathcal V$-small $\kappa$-filtered poset of such diagrams. Colimits of $D$-diagrams are computed pointwise. In each of these two categories the $\kappa$-presentable objects are closed under colimits of diagrams with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms. There are fixed $\mathcal U$-small families of $\mathcal U$-small representatives of the $\kappa$-presentable objects in each category, which are representative up to ordinary isomorphism in every $\mathcal V$. All these assertions use the same $\kappa$ and representatives under universe enlargement.

source.place: HTT A.3.3 proof, cardinal conditions (i)-(v), printed p.878; ordinary finitary simplicial-category presentation and its D-diagram version; A.3.6.18 universe-bound observation, p.905. proof.text: Describe a simplicial category by primary sorts $O$ and $M_n=\coprod_{a,b}A(a,b)_n$ for $n\geq0$. There are source and target maps $M_n\rightrightarrows O$, identity maps $O\to M_n$, face and degeneracy maps, and composition $M_n\times_O M_n\to M_n$. Specify the composable-pair pullbacks and the finite tuple sorts on which the category and simplicial equations are imposed. All operators fix objects and preserve identities and composition. This is a countable finite-limit sketch: take the category freely generated by these arrows and tuple arrows modulo the equations, specifying the finite tuple cones. Its models recover precisely the mapping fibers and their simplicial composition, and its model maps recover precisely arbitrary enriched functors, as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. For $D$-diagrams take one copy of these data per $d\in D$ and, per arrow $\alpha:d\to e$, maps on all primary sorts preserving the operations, with the identity and composition equations for $D$. Maps of these models are exactly ordinary natural transformations. This second sketch has fewer than $\kappa$ sorts and operations, since $|\operatorname{Mor}D|<\kappa$ and $\aleph_0<\kappa$. In each containing universe apply [lem-coef-finite-limit-model-presentability] to these small sketches: both categories are cocomplete and filtered colimits are computed on their sorts.

source.place: Kelly (1982), Section 9, (9.2), (9.4), (9.7), (9.8); the concrete simplicial-category and D-diagram signatures are written out here.

proof.text: Colimits in the diagram category are pointwise. For a small diagram $X:I\to\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathrm{sCat}_{\mathcal V})$, set $L(d)=\operatorname{colim}_iX_i(d)$. Each $\alpha:d\to e$ induces $L(\alpha)$ from the maps $X_i(d)\to X_i(e)\to L(e)$, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Uniqueness in this universal property gives $L(1)=1$ and $L(\beta\alpha)=L(\beta)L(\alpha)$. A compatible family $X_i\to Y$ gives unique maps $L(d)\to Y(d)$; their naturality follows by precomposing with every colimit coprojection, and their uniqueness follows in each value. Thus $L$ has exactly the colimit universal property. This also proves that evaluation preserves all these colimits.

source.place: Tag 002F, colimit universal property; explicit pointwise construction in an ordinary functor category.

proof.text: For either category call the disjoint union of its primary sorts its carrier; for a diagram this is the union over all $d$ of the carriers of its values. Suppose $P$ has carrier of cardinality less than $\kappa$, and let $X:I\to\mathcal C$ have $\mathcal V$-small $\kappa$-filtered index and colimit $L$. Step 1 computes $L$ on primary sorts. Since $\kappa$ is infinite, $I$ is filtered in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: cocones on the empty diagram, on two objects, and on a parallel pair (diagrams with finitely many morphisms) give a stage, a common receiving stage, and an equalizing arrow; so [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] applies to each sort. Given $f:P\to L$, choose a stage representative for the image of every primary element, using clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. There are fewer than $\kappa$ representatives. A cocone in $I$ on their discrete family puts them all at one stage $i$. First impose source and target preservation. Each required equality holds in $L$, so clause (3) of that node gives an arrow $i\to i_e$ witnessing it. There are fewer than $\kappa$ such equations. A cocone on this star-shaped diagram, which has fewer than $\kappa$ arrows, gives a single arrow $i\to j$ making all endpoint equalities hold. Thus every composable pair in $P$ has composable representatives at $j$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.3.3, cardinal conditions (i), (ii), (iv), printed p.878; explicit cardinal calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: At stage $j$, impose preservation of identities, faces, degeneracies, composition on every composable pair of $P$, and, for a $D$-diagram, every structure map. The set of these requirements has cardinality less than $\kappa$: there are fewer than $\kappa$ elements, fewer than $\kappa$ operations of finite arity, and a finite power of an infinite cardinal less than $\kappa$ is still less than $\kappa$. Regularity bounds their union. Every equation already holds in $L$. Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to each, and take a cocone on their star as in step 3. The resulting representatives preserve every displayed operation, hence define a morphism $P\to X_k$ factoring $f$. For two stage morphisms with the same image in $\operatorname{Hom}(P,L)$, first put them at a common stage. For each primary element their values become equal after an arrow by clause (3). One cocone on the fewer than $\kappa$ witnessing arrows makes the two morphisms equal on all primary sorts, hence equal. The same node's clauses (1) and (2), now for the set-valued diagram $\operatorname{Hom}(P,X_i)$, show that its comparison to $\operatorname{Hom}(P,L)$ is bijective. Thus $P$ is $\kappa$-presentable.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.3.3, cardinal conditions (i), (ii), (iv), printed p.878; explicit cardinal calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Let $F$ be an arbitrary object of either category. Starting with any fewer than $\kappa$ of its primary elements, repeatedly adjoin their endpoints, identity simplices, faces, degeneracies, composites of every composable pair already selected, and, for diagrams, the images under all arrows of $D$. At each round there are fewer than $\kappa$ outputs: the operations have finite arity, their number is less than $\kappa$, and regularity bounds the union over them. The countable union of the rounds still has size less than $\kappa$ because $\kappa$ is uncountable regular. Every finite tuple in the union occurs in one round, so its operation value occurs in the next. Restricting the operations of $F$ therefore gives a simplicial subcategory or a $D$-subdiagram, including every required identity and composite. All equations hold by restriction from $F$. No fullness on mapping sets is asserted. With empty input this constructs the empty subcategory, or the everywhere-empty subdiagram.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.3.3, cardinal conditions (i), (ii), (iv), printed p.878; explicit cardinal calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Let $B(F)$ be the poset of all substructures of $F$ obtained by selecting primary subsets closed under exactly the operations of step 5 and having total carrier size less than $\kappa$. It is $\mathcal V$-small: it is a subclass of the product of the power sets of the primary sorts of the $\mathcal V$-small structure $F$. It is nonempty by the empty substructure. For fewer than $\kappa$ members their primary union has size less than $\kappa$ by regularity; applying step 5 gives an upper bound in $B(F)$. Thus $B(F)$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Every primary element of $F$ lies in a member by starting with that element. Hence the diagram of inclusions has union $F$ on every primary sort. By the pointwise filtered-colimit assertion of [lem-coef-finite-limit-model-presentability], this inclusion cocone is colimiting. By step 4 all its objects are $\kappa$-presentable. This gives the required filtered-poset presentation, for simplicial categories as well as for diagrams.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.3.3, cardinal conditions (i), (ii), (iv), printed p.878; explicit cardinal calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $F$ is $\kappa$-presentable. Apply its Hom functor to the colimit of step 6. The identity $1_F$ comes from a map $r:F\to B$ for one $B\in B(F)$, with inclusion $u:B\to F$ satisfying $ur=1_F$. On every primary sort, $u$ is an inclusion and has a right inverse, so that inclusion is surjective and the primary subset equals the whole sort. Consequently the total carrier of $F$ has size less than $\kappa$, since that of $B$ does. Together with step 4, this proves the carrier-size characterization of presentability in both categories. In the simplicial-category case the carrier cardinal is exactly the size in the statement.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.3.3, cardinal conditions (i), (ii), (iv), printed p.878; explicit cardinal calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: For a $D$-diagram $F$, its total carrier has size less than $\kappa$ exactly when each value has size less than $\kappa$. One implication is inclusion of a summand; for the other, $|\operatorname{Ob}D|\leq|\operatorname{Mor}D|<\kappa$ because each object has its own identity, and regularity bounds the union of these carriers. Applying the simplicial-category characterization and the diagram characterization of step 7 gives exactly: $F$ is $\kappa$-presentable if and only if every $F(d)$ is $\kappa$-presentable. For empty $D$ the carrier is empty and this criterion correctly gives the unique object of the terminal diagram category.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.3.3, cardinal conditions (i), (ii), (iv), printed p.878; explicit cardinal calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] separately to the two categories. Their Hom sets are $\mathcal V$-small because morphisms are families of functions between their $\mathcal V$-small primary sorts satisfying equations. Each has the needed colimits by step 1. For a diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ indexing morphisms and $\kappa$-presentable values, the cited theorem says its colimit is $\kappa$-presentable. This proves both closure assertions, including the empty colimit. No assertion that arbitrary colimits are computed on primary sorts is used.

source.place: CategoryTheory.isCardinalPresentable_of_isColimit, lines 185-195; read source and reuse the existing Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Construct the common families in the smaller universe. Relabel the disjoint carrier of a structure of size less than $\kappa$ as a subset of the ordinal $\kappa$, retaining its partition into primary sorts. For diagrams retain the labels $d\in D$ as well. Each endpoint, simplicial operator, identity, composition and $D$-structure map is then coded by the graph of a function on a subset of a finite power of $\kappa$. The family of primary sorts and operation labels is $\mathcal U$-small. All these graphs and all families of them thus range over a fixed $\mathcal U$-small set, using power sets and products inside $\mathcal U$. Restrict to codes satisfying the equations and having total carrier size less than $\kappa$. Each code is an actual $\mathcal U$-small simplicial category or diagram. For any containing $\mathcal V$, relabelling any structure there of size less than $\kappa$ produces one of exactly these codes: its transported graphs are subsets of the same $\mathcal U$-sets, and hence belong to $\mathcal U$. This supplies a single $\mathcal U$-small covering family for each category, valid in every $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.3.3.3, cardinal conditions (i), (ii), (iv), printed p.878; explicit cardinal calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: If representatives are required without repetition, choose one member of each ordinary-isomorphism class of the coded family inside $\mathcal U$. Isomorphisms between two codes are just bijections of their primary sets preserving all operations. Every possible such family of bijections is already an element of a fixed $\mathcal U$-small product of function sets; thus enlargement to $\mathcal V$ introduces no new isomorphisms between codes. The chosen representatives therefore still cover in every $\mathcal V$. Relabel the bounded substructures in the presentation of step 6 by these representatives; conjugating each inclusion by the chosen isomorphisms gives a diagram on the same small filtered poset and an isomorphic colimiting cocone. The small presentable families now generate each category under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, so cocompleteness from step 1 proves local $\kappa$-presentability. Every construction used the originally fixed $\kappa$, the same countable signature and the same $D$; no replacement cardinal was chosen. This proves the asserted uniformity.
